intent: Investigate pacman freezing at its first PreTransaction hook, and repair the deployment defects the investigation exposed: a stale pacman wrapper that no check could see, a half-finished guard-lib migration, and unserialised heavy jobs on a 7.6 GB machine.
scope: NON-GOAL: a pacman-side fix for the stall - it could not be reproduced, so there is no verified defect to fix
NON-GOAL: the shutdown-schedule guard instance (/etc/shutdown-schedule.conf absent on this machine)
changes: Established from /var/log/pacman.log that the stall hit 5 transactions since 2026-07-29, always at the FIRST PreTransaction hook (4/56 guard-lib runs, plus 1/142 hosts-hook runs from when THAT hook was first). What the failures share is position, not identity.
Proved the guard-lib hook is not the cause: /etc/guard-lib/targets is empty since install, so the loop body never executes and the script reaches exit 0 in milliseconds.

New diagnose_pacman_hook_stall.sh: drives real transactions (reinstalling the 0-file base-devel meta-package from cache), with a watchdog that dumps /proc/<pid>/{stack,wchan,syscall,status}, the process tree, meminfo and PSI when a live pacman sits on a hook line; --with-load applies memory pressure; --watch passively captures a real stall.
Redeployed the pacman wrapper: 19916 B -> 27515 B. The old copy had its own inline stale-lock handler but never sourced the shared pacman_lock_lib.sh that makepkg_wrapper already used.

Both installers now write a drift manifest (absolute paths) covering source AND installed hashes; check_and_enable_services.sh replays it with sha256sum -c and fails closed when the manifest is missing.

New migrate_hosts_guard_to_guard_lib.sh: registers hosts/nsswitch/resolved as guardctl file-guard instances, installs plugins to a stable /usr/local/share path (guardctl records absolute plugin paths), retires the legacy hooks and units, and provides --rollback/--status/--dry-run.
New heavy_job_lock.sh: one system-wide flock shared between root and the user, serialising pacman transactions, makepkg builds and the coverage hook; names the current holder; always fails open.

verification.evidence: 2578 MB hog, MemAvailable -> 1657 MB; 25 transactions, 0 stalls, 4/4/8 s. NOT a reproduction: 65 clean runs against a historical 7% rate is ~0.9% likely, so the trigger is conditional on something this synthetic load does not recreate. Memory pressure is neither confirmed nor refuted.

verification.command: sudo check_and_enable_services.sh --status, across five induced states
verification.evidence: clean -> no drift; repo source edited -> detected; deployed file tampered -> detected; restored -> clean; manifest removed -> 'deployed version unverifiable' (fails closed)

3 instances registered; /etc/hosts byte-identical (171441 lines), chattr +i, ro bind mount intact, www.youtube.com -> 0.0.0.0, root write refused with EPERM; only ONE PreTransaction hook now and transactions dropped from ~5-6 s to ~3-4 s; rollback restores hooks, units, +i and the bind mount

--fail-fast returns 75 naming the holder; waiting mode started job B 0.01 s after job A ended; unusable lock path runs the command anyway (fail open); with the wrapper deployed, `pacman -Q` took 0 s while a real -U transaction waited 18 s behind a held lock
shellcheck, codespell, secrets, binary-block, polling-anti-pattern all Passed; only the evidence/contract hooks failed, which this artifact and its contract resolve

risks: The stall is NOT fixed - it is only instrumented. --watch must capture a real occurrence before any pacman-side change is justified.

The drift manifest currently records paths inside the git worktree this work was done in. Both installers must be re-run from ~/testsAndMisc after merging, or the check will report permanent drift once the worktree is removed.
Retiring the legacy hosts-guard layer means /etc/hosts protection now depends entirely on guard-lib; --rollback is the escape hatch and has been exercised.

Two bugs were found ONLY by running --rollback: fg_uninstall clears chattr +i on its way out (legacy watchers only fire on PathModified), and a `((i > 20)) && break` left the loop body's status at 1, which under set -e silently aborted the rollback - but only when the loop actually ran, so --dry-run looked healthy. Both fixed; both had briefly left /etc/hosts unprotected.
A pacman transaction can now wait up to 30 minutes behind a build before failing open. Read-only queries are deliberately exempt.
rollback: guard-lib migration: sudo migrate_hosts_guard_to_guard_lib.sh --rollback, then confirm lsattr /etc/hosts shows 'i' and findmnt shows the ro bind mount
pacman wrapper: sudo ln -sfn /usr/bin/pacman.orig /usr/bin/pacman bypasses the wrapper entirely; pre-change copies are in the session scratchpad
heavy-job lock: rm /etc/tmpfiles.d/heavy-job-lock.conf /run/heavy-job.lock - every call site fails open when the lock is absent
After any rollback, validate: pacman -Q works, a real -U transaction completes, getent hosts www.youtube.com still returns 0.0.0.0, and /etc/hosts is still 171441 lines
